/itineraryStops/3/smartNotes/facilities.source_en: On-island restaurants serve Korean comfort food (hotteok, sweet potato latte, tteok-galbi). Sonata Cafe in a traditional hanok is the signature stop. Foreign-card-friendly ticket counter at Gapyeong Wharf — ticket machines do not accept foreign cards, ask at the counter.
/itineraryStops/3/smartNotes/facilities.tm: I ristoranti dell’isola servono piatti coreani di conforto (hotteok, latte alla patata dolce, tteok-galbi). Il Sonata Cafe, in una casa tradizionale hanok, è la sosta simbolo. Al molo di Gapyeong la biglietteria accetta le carte straniere: le macchine automatiche no, quindi si rivolga allo sportello.

/itineraryStops/3/whyOnRoute.source_en: Nami sits in the middle of the day because it is the one stop that needs both daylight and a boat. The metasequoia and ginkgo avenues under frost are what the island is worth crossing for in winter, and they need light; the ferry deck is also exposed, so a mid-afternoon crossing is more comfortable than a late one. Placing it after Seoraksan also breaks the long westward drive into two manageable legs rather than one.

/itineraryStops/3/convenience/parking.source_en: Gapyeong Wharf 6,000 KRW small car / 10,000 KRW large vehicle
/itineraryStops/3/convenience/parking.tm: Molo di Gapyeong: 6.000 KRW per le auto piccole / 10.000 KRW per i veicoli grandi

/itineraryStops/3/convenience/restroom.source_en: Multiple on island and at Gapyeong Wharf
/itineraryStops/3/convenience/restroom.tm: Diversi sull’isola e al molo di Gapyeong

/itineraryStops/3/description.source_en:
Nami Island opens the day's second chapter with a 5-minute ferry crossing from Gapyeong Wharf onto a half-moon-shaped river island in the Bukhan River. Approximately **460,000 m² (140,000 pyeong) and ~5 km in circumference**, Namiseom is named after **General Nami (Nam Yi, 1441-1468)**, a Joseon-era military commander executed at age 28 after being falsely accused of treason during the reign of King Yejong. 

The island originally became land only during floods; **in 1944 the Japanese colonial government built the Cheongpyeong Dam, raising the river level and making Nami a permanent island**. It found global fame **in 2002 as the filming location for KBS drama 'Winter Sonata'** starring Bae Yong-joon and Choi Ji-woo — the catalyst for the early 2000s Hallyu wave — and continues to draw about **3.3 million visitors annually (1.3 million foreign)**, making it Korea's most-visited single tourist destination after Seoul, Busan, and Jeju. 

Since **March 1, 2006** the island has branded itself as the self-declared **'Naminara Republic'** with its own flag, currency (Nami Tongbo coins), passport, and postal service — a tourism marketing concept rather than an actual political entity. 

The signature **Metasequoia tree-lined avenue** (Winter Sonata's iconic snowy lane), the **Riverside Lover's Ginkgo Tree Lane** on the south side, the **Korean Pine Road**, and the recycled-glass **Sequoia Bridge** made from soju bottles are all walkable in a relaxed two hours. On-island wildlife includes peacocks (including rare albinos), ostriches, wild rabbits, and squirrels. 

**The Naminara Republic VISA Fee (round-trip ferry included) is included in this tour price**.
/itineraryStops/3/description.tm:
L’isola di Nami apre il secondo capitolo della giornata con una traversata in traghetto di 5 minuti dal molo di Gapyeong verso un’isola fluviale a mezzaluna, sul fiume Bukhan. Di circa **460.000 m² (140.000 pyeong) e ~5 km di perimetro**, Namiseom prende il nome dal **generale Nami (Nam Yi, 1441-1468)**, comandante militare di epoca Joseon giustiziato a 28 anni dopo essere stato falsamente accusato di tradimento sotto il regno di re Yejong. 

In origine l’isola emergeva soltanto durante le piene; **nel 1944 il governo coloniale giapponese costruì la diga di Cheongpyeong, innalzando il livello del fiume e rendendo Nami un’isola permanente**. La fama mondiale arrivò **nel 2002, come luogo di ripresa della serie KBS «Winter Sonata»** con Bae Yong-joon e Choi Ji-woo — la scintilla dell’onda hallyu dei primi anni 2000 — e ancora oggi l’isola attira circa **3,3 milioni di visitatori l’anno (1,3 milioni stranieri)**, il che la rende la singola destinazione turistica più visitata della Corea dopo Seoul, Busan e Jeju. 

Dal **1º marzo 2006** l’isola si presenta come autoproclamata **«Repubblica di Naminara»**, con bandiera, moneta (le monete Nami Tongbo), passaporto e servizio postale propri: una trovata di marketing turistico, non un’entità politica reale. 

Il celebre **viale alberato di metasequoie** (la strada innevata iconica di Winter Sonata), il **viale dei ginkgo degli innamorati** lungo il fiume, sul lato sud, la **strada dei pini coreani** e il **ponte delle sequoie** in vetro riciclato, ricavato da bottiglie di soju, si percorrono tutti a piedi in due ore tranquille. Fra la fauna dell’isola: pavoni (compresi rari esemplari albini), struzzi, conigli selvatici e scoiattoli. 

**Il «visto» della Repubblica di Naminara (traghetto andata e ritorno compreso) è incluso nel prezzo di questo tour**.

/itineraryStops/3/visitBasics/hours.source_en: Ferry from 08:00, last boat in at 21:00, roughly every 10-20 minutes through the day; most on-island shops close by 18:00. Winter schedules can change with weather

/itineraryStops/3/visitBasics/walking.source_en: Easy — flat tree-lined paths, though they can be icy underfoot in midwinter. The half-perimeter walk is ~3 km. Bicycle and e-buggy rental is available on the island at your own expense

/itineraryStops/3/visitBasics/admission.source_en: Naminara Republic visa fee, round-trip ferry included: Adult ₩19,000 — INCLUDED in this tour

/itineraryStops/4/timeUsed/0.source_en: Coach parks and the guide walks the group to the valley entrance (~10 min)

/itineraryStops/4/timeUsed/1.source_en: Deck path to the ice-wall viewing area and photographs (~25 min)

/itineraryStops/4/timeUsed/2.source_en: Optional sledding or greenhouse garden, or back to the coach early to warm up (~10 min)

/itineraryStops/4/highlights/0.source_en: An ice wall reported at around 25 m, grown on the valley rock face by villagers of Garil 2-ri since winter 2023 — built, not natural

/itineraryStops/4/highlights/1.source_en: Run by the village residents' association (about 30 people) as an off-season project, branded 어비계곡 겨울나라, 'Eobi Valley Winter Wonderland'

/itineraryStops/4/highlights/2.source_en: Wooden deck viewing path with night lighting, added under Gyeonggi Province's clean-valley restoration scheme

/itineraryStops/4/highlights/3.source_en: Ice sledding, a spinning snow sled, an igloo photo zone and a heated greenhouse garden alongside the wall

/itineraryStops/4/highlights/4.source_en: The valley's name 어비 (魚飛) means 'flying fish' — from water once fast enough to make fish appear to fly

/itineraryStops/4/highlights/5.source_en: Visitor numbers roughly doubled to about 60,000 in a season as word spread, mostly among Southeast Asian travellers

/itineraryStops/4/smartNotes/tip.source_en: Wear non-slip winter footwear and treat the ice wall as weather-dependent rather than guaranteed — a warm spell shrinks it and the village decides its own opening. Bring small cash for the on-site fees.

/itineraryStops/4/smartNotes/facilities.source_en: Village-run and basic: a heated greenhouse garden, sled slope and small stalls. Do not count on substantial food or extensive indoor warm-up space.

/itineraryStops/4/whyOnRoute.source_en: Eobi closes the day for two reasons. Geographically it is the only stop on the Seoul side of the route — Seorak-myeon sits in southern Gapyeong, already pointing home — so an hour here costs no extra driving at the end of a long day. Editorially it is the reason this itinerary is a winter product rather than a year-round one: Seoraksan and Nami can be visited in any season, but the ice wall exists for perhaps eight weeks, and only if the cold holds. It is also the stop most travellers have never heard of, which is a good note to end on.
